structured.approach: I read the five contracted inputs: feat.fitment, feat.intake, org.templates, org.strategy_capability and org.decision_log. I also read two approved background outputs with context_get: feat.classification and feat.prebacklog. I read the source ticket file (requirements/ZD-48600.md) and the feature COMMUNICATION.md. I drafted the BRD in the org.templates section order: problem, business outcome, users, scope, out of scope, business rules, success measures, approvals. The org.templates file holds no business question set, so I ran one from the template sections plus the open points from REQ-01 to REQ-03. Each question is answered from an input or marked "Not answered". I added a validation check section covering template conformance, a citation for every requirement, the decision log conflict check, consistency with approved outputs, and number provenance. An independent verifier then checked the draft. It found 6 unsupported statements and 5 weaker citation problems: an overstated "only new functions", BR-3 stated as a rule when the source records it as an assumption, an uncited Domain SME approver, an overbroad problem statement, an incomplete number list, and a claim that org.templates names a question set. I fixed all 11 before finishing. I left the strategy-fit and audit questions open for the Leadership gate and did not resolve them myself.

claims.text: The business need is that AP managers want to see which overdue invoices belong to vendors that usually pay late, so they can chase them first.
The BRD follows the template sections problem, business outcome, users, scope, out of scope, business rules, success measures and approvals.
The fitment verdict is Yes with reason code FIT-YES-ROADMAP, linked to R-AP-12 'give AP managers earlier visibility of overdue payables', and PM and Leadership approved REQ-03.
The overdue list covers unpaid invoices more than 30 days past due, sorted by days descending then id, with risk 'unknown' for vendors not in risk_by_vendor.
Vendor risk is 'high' when predict_delay_days(history) > 30, 'medium' when it is > 10, otherwise 'low'; the boundaries must be tested explicitly.

Paid invoices are excluded from aging (D-2026-050), monetary amounts use Decimal, never float (D-2026-044), and aging buckets use calendar days after due date (D-2026-031); the BRD has no conflict with these decisions.
The change has no finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution; it is tier T2 and the risk label is advisory only.

The documented AP capability is that the ap_aging service computes aging buckets (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+) for open invoices; the strategy is to help finance teams pay on time and avoid late-payment penalties, and auditability and traceability are core product promises.
No input links this entry to the strategy of paying on time, and whether the risk label and the data behind it must be auditable is undecided; both are carried forward from OQ-F1 and OQ-F3.
Related items ZD-48211, ZD-48501, ZD-48470, PROV-ACME-2026-11 and ZD-48377 raise sequencing questions; they were kept separate, not merged.
The context catalogue lists org.templates as holding a business question set, but the file contains only the template section lists.
No regulatory source applies to this change, so no requirement carries a regulation section or page.

open_questions: OQ-B1 (PM / Leadership): What do 'vendors that usually pay late' and 'chase them first' mean for an AP (payables) module, and does the entry serve the strategy 'help finance teams pay on time and avoid late-payment penalties'? (carries OQ-F1)
OQ-B2 (Leadership): Should a business rule require the vendor risk label, and the delay history and predicted delay behind it, to be recorded or explainable for audit? (carries OQ-F3)
OQ-B3 (PM / Leadership): Which business KPI should measure success beyond the end-to-end proof? The inputs give none.

OQ-B4 (PM): Edge-case rules the ticket does not define: day unit and early payments in delay_days, paid/paid_date disagreement, risk for an empty history, and HTML-escaping in the portal table (carries OQ-2, OQ-4, OQ-5, OQ-6).
OQ-B5 (PM): Are there users besides AP managers?
OQ-B6 (PM): Sequencing with ZD-48211/ZD-48501 (shared overdue rule), ZD-48470 (feed v2/v3), PROV-ACME-2026-11 (explanation request shape) and ZD-48377 (exactly-30-days fix).
OQ-B7 (PM): Is there an approved business question set for BRD preparation? The org.templates file holds none.
structured.summary: I wrote the BRD for FEAT-ZD-48600 at outputs/FEAT-ZD-48600/feat.brd.md, ready for the Leadership gate. It covers all eight template sections. Scope has 7 items (S-1 to S-7), one per change request CR-1 to CR-7. There are 12 cited business rules: the overdue rule is 'unpaid and more than 30 days past due'; risk is 'high' above 30, 'medium' above 10, 'low' otherwise, and 'unknown' when no risk is available; the list is sorted by days and then id; amounts are Decimal and shown to two decimals; and the label is advisory only. The 5 success measures are the end-to-end proof, the boundary-day tests, no float conversion, unchanged signatures, and paid invoices excluded. The document also has a business question set and a validation check. The check found no conflict with D-2026-031, D-2026-044 or D-2026-050. An independent verifier flagged 11 grounding issues, and I fixed all of them. Strategy fit, audit needs, business KPIs, edge cases and sequencing remain non-blocking open questions for Leadership and the PM.
